persons.dossier: Marie Curie investigated radioactivity through physics and chemistry. Born in Warsaw, she later worked in Paris. Research with Pierre Curie identified polonium and radium. The name polonium referred to the country of her birth. She later held a physics professorship at the Sorbonne. Her Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded in 1911. This passage concerns publicly documented research and professional life; it does not describe private memories or provide a hidden symbol.

persons.dossier: C. V. Raman investigated the scattering of light. His work examined light after it interacted with matter. Some scattered light has a different frequency from the incoming light. Raman received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930. This passage describes public observations about light, not private thoughts or a hidden symbol.

persons.dossier: Barbara McClintock studied genetics using maize plants. She followed inherited traits across successive generations. These findings challenged the idea that genetic elements always remain in fixed positions. McClintock received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1983. This passage concerns public research findings, not access to her private thoughts or a hidden symbol.
